content.user_title: Modernize React Apps With Hooks and React 18
content.value_statement: Legacy React code can slow upgrades, testing, and performance work. This skill guides class-to-hooks migrations, React 18 adoption, TypeScript conversion, and codemod planning.
actual_capabilities: Plan React version upgrades from older releases to React 18 patterns.
Convert class component state, lifecycle methods, and context usage to hooks.
Guide adoption of createRoot, automatic batching, transitions, and Suspense patterns.
Recommend codemod workflows for repetitive React refactors.
Add TypeScript typing patterns for components and generic lists.
Review performance opportunities using memoization and code splitting.
limitations: It does not automatically verify every dependency compatibility issue.
It needs project context, test results, and upgrade goals for precise guidance.
Codemod suggestions still require human review before merge.
It does not replace React release notes or framework-specific migration guides.

use_cases.title: Upgrade Planning
use_cases.description: Create an incremental React upgrade plan with risks, testing checkpoints, and rollout steps.

use_cases.title: Hooks Migration
use_cases.description: Convert class components to functional components while preserving lifecycle behavior and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Performance Review
use_cases.description: Identify useful React 18, memoization, and code-splitting improvements for a production interface.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a React application upgrade path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React project context and propose an incremental modernization plan. Include version steps, likely risks, and validation checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate class-to-hooks migration for one component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this class component to a functional component with hooks. Preserve state behavior, lifecycle timing, cleanup, and public props.

prompt_templates.title: Adopt React 18 Features
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration to concurrent-friendly React patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React 17 code and recommend React 18 changes. Cover root setup, StrictMode effects, batching, transitions, Suspense, and test updates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Codemod Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor planning across a larger codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a codemod-assisted migration plan for this React codebase. Include candidate transformations, manual review steps, rollback points, and verification tasks.

output_examples.input: A team needs to move a React 16 app toward React 18 without a full rewrite.
output_examples.output: A staged upgrade plan that starts with dependency review, then React 17 compatibility, React 18 root changes, StrictMode fixes, and focused regression tests.

output_examples.input: A class component uses state, mount logic, update logic, and cleanup.
output_examples.output: A migration explanation that maps state to hooks, moves lifecycle behavior into effects, preserves cleanup, and lists behavior to test.

output_examples.input: A dashboard has slow list rendering after a modernization pass.
output_examples.output: A performance review that checks render causes, memoization value, callback stability, code splitting, and measurable before-and-after validation.

best_practices: Upgrade incrementally and keep each change tied to a testable checkpoint.
Start hooks migrations with simple leaf components before shared containers.
Measure performance before adding memoization or code splitting.
anti_patterns: Migrating every component at once without staged validation.
Adding hooks mechanically without checking lifecycle behavior and cleanup.
Running codemods without review, tests, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Can this skill upgrade a full React app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans, patterns, and review guidance. A developer still applies changes and validates behavior.

faq.question: Does it support React 18 migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers createRoot, batching, StrictMode effects, transitions, Suspense, and related testing concerns.

faq.question: Can it help convert class components to hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps state, lifecycle methods, context, cleanup, and reusable logic to hooks.

faq.question: Does it include codemod guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests codemod workflows for repetitive changes and stresses review before merging generated edits.

faq.question: Is it useful for TypeScript migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes component prop typing and generic component patterns for React code.

faq.question: What inputs make results better?
faq.answer: Provide current React version, framework, package constraints, representative components, test coverage, and upgrade goals.
